dailyInsight.headline: Audit the narrower environment after the broader thread changes
dailyInsight.insight: Codex now gives a ready environment attachment a resolved permission profile of its own instead of treating the thread as the only authority. Builders and operators who select remote, sandboxed, or otherwise distinct environments inside a write-capable coding session should audit one disposable path: after selecting a read-only attachment, try a harmless write there, update the thread settings, and confirm the attachment remains read-only.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The reported Codex change puts the complete permission profile in `EnvironmentConfig`, lets a `Ready` attachment override thread permissions while `FromThread` selections inherit them, and adds a remote-environment test in which a write-capable thread receives `WRITE_DENIED` from a selected read-only environment. A follow-up retains the source of configuration ownership so later thread updates refresh inherited attachments without overwriting attachment-owned permissions and capability roots.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A multi-environment agent session can otherwise look safe at the thread level while a stricter attachment silently inherits a broader setting. A bounded write-denial test checks the useful property directly: the selected environment keeps the authority promised by its own configuration even when the parent session changes.

actions.audience: Builder or operator of a coding-agent workflow that selects a remote, sandboxed, or alternate environment within a write-capable session
actions.label: Check one attachment-owned read-only boundary
actions.instruction: In a disposable workspace with no production credentials, start a thread that can write, select one environment configured read-only, and attempt one harmless marker-file write there. Change a thread-level setting or refresh the selection and repeat. Verify that the selected environment reports denial and creates no file; record which setting source owns the attachment. Do not use destructive commands or broad filesystem permissions.

receipts.title: Honor per-environment permission profiles (#38673)
receipts.supports: Shows the resolved per-environment permission profile, the ready-versus-thread inheritance behavior, and a focused test proving a selected read-only attachment blocks a write from an otherwise write-capable thread.

receipts.title: Preserve environment configuration ownership (#38678)
receipts.supports: Shows the ownership rule for later thread-setting updates: inherited attachments refresh while ready, attachment-owned permission profiles and capability roots remain in effect.

confidence.basis: Two fresh public Codex implementation receipts and a focused remote-environment regression test agree on a narrow configuration-ownership contract. The recommendation is a reversible audit of that source behavior, not a claim about a released client, every environment provider, or production enforcement.

dailyInsight.limitation: These main-branch receipts do not establish a shipped release, remote-environment availability, credential isolation, network-policy behavior, independent security review, or equivalent behavior in other agent runtimes. A read-only attachment test is one boundary check, not a complete threat model.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public integration tests or documented runtime paths show a selected ready attachment with a read-only profile can write after a thread settings update, reconnect, replacement, or child-thread transition without an explicit permission change.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for release notes and integration coverage that exercise reconnects, attachment replacement, child threads, capability roots, credentials, and network policy under the new ownership rule.
